title: Acid–base equilibrium in analysis
basic_overview: Ka, Kb, pKa, buffers and hydrolysis govern analytical acid–base calculations.

extra_info_content.short_trick: At half-equivalence for weak acid/strong base: pH=pKa.
extra_info_content.step_by_step: 1. Write Ka/Kb. 2. Check approximation. 3. Use Henderson–Hasselbalch in buffer region. 4. At equivalence use conjugate hydrolysis.
extra_info_content.factors: Do not use buffer equations outside their valid regime.
extra_info_content.kinetics_or_energy: Compare thermodynamic driving force with kinetic barrier when relevant; do not treat a favourable ΔG° as proof of a fast reaction.
